issue_context.title: Rescue tasks are run after a role called with import_role or include_role
issue_context.body:
<!--- Verify first that your issue is not already reported on GitHub -->
<!--- Also test if the latest release and devel branch are affected too -->
<!--- Complete *all* sections as described, this form is processed automatically -->

##### SUMMARY
<!--- Explain the problem briefly below -->
Block + Rescue behavior is unexpected when the Rescue is inside of a role that is called with import_role or include_role. The Rescue tasks are called *after* the role completes.


##### ISSUE TYPE
- Bug Report

##### COMPONENT NAME
<!--- Write the short name of the module, plugin, task or feature below, use your best guess if unsure -->
import_role
include_role

##### ANSIBLE VERSION
<!--- Paste verbatim output from "ansible --version" between quotes -->
```paste below
ansible 2.9.0
  config file = /etc/ansible/ansible.cfg
  configured module search path = ['/home/michael/.ansible/plugins/modules', '/usr/share/ansible/plugins/modules']
  ansible python module location = /usr/lib/python3.7/site-packages/ansible
  executable location = /usr/bin/ansible
  python version = 3.7.5 (default, Oct 17 2019, 12:16:48) [GCC 9.2.1 20190827 (Red Hat 9.2.1-1)]
```
This bug has occurred since at least 2.8.

##### CONFIGURATION
<!--- Paste verbatim output from "ansible-config dump --only-changed" between quotes -->
```paste below
none
```

##### OS / ENVIRONMENT
<!--- Provide all relevant information below, e.g. target OS versions, network device firmware, etc. -->
Occurs in Fedora or RHEL or Ansible Tower.


##### STEPS TO REPRODUCE
<!--- Describe exactly how to reproduce the problem, using a minimal test-case -->

<!--- Paste example playbooks or commands between quotes below -->
```yaml
inventory
---------
[test_inv]
h1
h2

role test
---------
- name: FIRST
  debug: msg="first {{ lookup('pipe', 'date -Is') }}"

- block:
   - fail:
     when: inventory_hostname == 'h1'
  rescue:
    - pause:
        seconds: 5
    - name: SECOND
      debug: msg="second {{ lookup('pipe', 'date -Is') }}"

- name: THIRD
  debug: msg="third {{ lookup('pipe', 'date -Is') }}"
- name: FOURTH
  debug: msg="fourth {{ lookup('pipe', 'date -Is') }}"


playbook with roles and working
-------------------------------
- hosts: test_inv
  gather_facts: false
  roles:
    - test 

playbook with import_role and task executed in wrong order
----------------------------------------------------------
- hosts: test_inv
  gather_facts: false
  tasks:
    - import_role:
        name: test 
```

(ctrl+C then 'C' = continue early, ctrl+C then 'A' = abort)
h1 | SUCCESS => {"changed": false, "delta": 5, "echo": true, "rc": 0, "start": "2019-11-16 00:32:19.984584", "stderr": "", "stdout": "Paused for 5.0 seconds", "stop": "2019-11-16 00:32:24.984690", "user_input": ""}

h1 | SUCCESS => {    "changed": false,     "msg": "third 2019-11-16T00:32:25,018989962+01:00"}
h2 | SUCCESS => {    "changed": false,     "msg": "third 2019-11-16T00:32:25,024043908+01:00"}
h1 | SUCCESS => {    "changed": false,     "msg": "fourth 2019-11-16T00:32:25,043906428+01:00"}
h2 | SUCCESS => {    "changed": false,     "msg": "fourth 2019-11-16T00:32:25,049696619+01:00"}

<!--- boilerplate: components_banner --->

Note for myself or anyone looking into this further:

The reason that it is working for `- role` and not for `{import, include}_role` appears to be that the latter implicitly wraps role's tasks into a block. That additional level seems to be problematic in the linear strategy for the `_get_next_task_lockstep` method which incorrectly inserts `noop` tasks resulting in the tasks being executed in the incorrect order.

Files identified in the description:
* [`lib/ansible/modules/import_role.py`](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/modules/import_role.py)
* [`lib/ansible/playbook/role/include.py`](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/lib/ansible/playbook/role/include.py)

review_comments: We still don't evaluate the conditional for flush_handlers, is there a reason not to warn in that case?
I meant to add the conditional evaluation to `flush_handlers` but apparently I forgot. Do you think we should not do that?
Oh. I'd be in favor of checking the conditional.
Done.

In this playbook, only the non-failed host executes the task after clear_host_errors:
```yaml
---
- hosts: localhost
  gather_facts: no
  tasks:
    - add_host: name={{ item }} ansible_connection=local
      loop: [h1, h2]

- hosts: h1,h2
  gather_facts: no
  handlers:
    - name: sometimes_fail
      fail:
      when: 'inventory_hostname == "h1"'
  tasks:
    - command: echo
      notify: sometimes_fail
    - meta: flush_handlers
    - meta: clear_host_errors
    - debug: msg='should run for both hosts'
```

This seems to fix it:
```suggestion
        if state.fail_state == FailedStates.HANDLERS:
            state.run_state = state.pre_flushing_run_state
            state.pre_flushing_run_state = None

        state.fail_state = FailedStates.NONE
```

Actually. The behavior in this PR (for handler failure/task failure) is the same as failure in a normal task on devel. Not sure if this is just unintuitive to me alone or a bug, but not something that needs to be addressed in this PR.

After thinking about it more, making a handler failure recoverable via clear_host_errors doesn't make sense since it's the last iterator state. Having a flush_handlers midplay is confusing me.
Although I wonder if we should think of this as clear_host_errors issue and deal with it in a separate PR?

Pushed https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/77955/commits/8fa40982a960b70eb8341e3e8ebd4146a27c6451 as a fix, probably needs a test too. We'll see if `ci_complete` passes.

Nice find!
`ci_complete` passed on the above commit and I added a test for it.
https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/77955/files#r942935468 is resolved in this PR.

To correct my initial comment in the thread - clear_host_errors works across plays currently (just like refresh_inventory). The documentation is ambiguous about how it should work, but rather than "fixing" prematurely and painting us into a corner, we decided it should just mirror the existing behavior.
I thought it could use a note in the changelog, but I don't see how run_handlers would have returned False. I guess this was unused?

Yeah, the return value of `run_handlers` was effectively hardcoded to `RUN_OK`. However I think you still have a point because since we now run handlers through strategies they affect the return value of each strategy which will be different from devel.
There seems to be no change in behavior. There is a check below for failed hosts and there the `result` (and subsequently the return code) is changed to be non-zero so I think we're good here.
Okay. It *looked* like a change in behavior, but I couldn't find one when tracing the code either. Thanks for checking.
We still don't evaluate the conditional for flush_handlers, is there a reason not to warn in that case?
I meant to add the conditional evaluation to `flush_handlers` but apparently I forgot. Do you think we should not do that?
Oh. I'd be in favor of checking the conditional.
